verses.1: My soul is weary within me; I will let my complaints fall upon Him. I will speak bitterly, my soul enduring.
verses.2: I say to God, Do not judge me. Show me what it is You contend with me for.
verses.3: Is it good for You to oppress, to despise the work of Your hands, and to favor the plans of the wicked?
verses.4: Are the eyes of a mortal like Yours? Do You look at a human as one might look at another human?
verses.5: Is the span of a human life Your life? Are the days of a human like Your days?
verses.6: For You have sought my iniquity and searched for my sin.
verses.7: For You know that I am innocent, yet who can snatch me from Your hand?
verses.8: Your hands formed me and made me; yet afterward You turned and crushed me.
verses.9: Recall now, that You made me like clay, and to dust You will return me.
verses.10: Were I not made like milk, and like cheese You have curdled me?
verses.11: You clothed me with skin and flesh, and with bones and sinews You wove me together.
verses.12: You gave me life and steadfast love, and Your care preserved my spirit.
verses.13: These things You have hidden in Your heart, I know—indeed, all of these are with You.
verses.14: If I sinned, You still watched over me, and from my iniquity You have not cleansed me.
verses.15: If I was guilty, woe is me! If I was righteous, I cannot lift up my head; I am full of disgrace and see my misery.
verses.16: Like a lion You hunt me for slaughter, and You turn again and strike me down.
verses.17: You renew Your witnesses before me, multiplying Your arrows against me, and You heap up attacks on me.
verses.18: Why then did You bring me forth from the womb? I would have perished, and no eye would have seen me.
verses.19: I would have been as though I had never been—why was I brought forth from the womb to die and cast into the grave?
verses.20: Are my days not few? Let them be done, and let me be released for a little while.
verses.21: Before I go, and do not return, to the land of darkness and shadow,
verses.22: to the land of eternal darkness, where there is no light and no eye can see a living soul.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "I will let my complaints fall upon Him" — captures the nuance of "I will release my words to Him" from the source's "עֲפַשׂאָה".
- v. 4: "Are the eyes of a mortal like Yours?" — the source uses a Hebrew idiom, "the eyes of flesh are to You" which is rephrased for clarity.
- v. 15: "I am full of disgrace and see my misery" — "שְׂבַע קָלוֹן" is a figurative expression meaning "full of shame," rendered naturally.
- v. 22: "where there is no light and no eye can see a living soul" — the Hebrew "צַלְמָוֶת" is interpreted as "eternal darkness" to align with the context of the grave.
